transcription: My grandma accidentally joined a sorority group chat and became their life coach. This started with a wrong number. That's it. A whole accidental chain of chaos started because my 76-year-old grandma got a text meant for a college group chat. Some freshmen at the university near her house accidentally typed one digit wrong when making a group chat for her sorority's new pledges, and that digit happened to be Nana Jones. Instead of leaving the chat like a normal person, my grandma responded with that alone should have been the end. But for some reason, instead of removing her, they responded and she did. Cut to two weeks later my grandma is fully invested in the drama of this sorority she's never met. She's giving advice on outfits for their mixer where the black one, but not with those shoes, telling one girl to break up with her situation ship because a man who can't remember your dog's name doesn't deserve your weekend, and even helping someone write a breakup text like she was ghostwriting for the bachelor. At one point she sent them a pick of a casserole she made and said if any of you are ever hungry I'll leave some on the porch. They actually went. This group of 18 to 20-something-year-old started going over to her house to hang out, eat her lasagna, and listen to her stories. They brought her flowers once. She cried. One girl got dumped and ended up crying in my grandma's kitchen while Nana June fed her cookies and told her the story of her own divorce back when men still wore hats. They now call her glamour. I only found out about any of this when I visited her last weekend and she casually said, could you help me set up Spotify? I promise the girls would make a playlist for their pre-game. Pre-game.
